questions.question: A ________ government governs within the bounds established by constitutional law and citizen rights.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Democratic.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **democratic government**, power is derived from the consent of the governed.
 
• It operates according to the principles set out in a constitution.
 
• important factors of democracy includes: **rule of law, Protection of Rights, Separation of Powers, Regular Elections and so on.**
 
• There are two types of democracy:
 
 
• **Direct Democracy**: Citizens directly participate in decision-making (e.g., referendums).
 
• **Representative Democracy**: Citizens elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **dictatorship** is a form of government in which absolute power is concentrated in a single leader or a small group.
 
• key factors includes: **Centralized Power**, **Lack of Political Freedom**, **Suppression of Dissent**, **Control Over Media**, **Limited Civil Liberties**, **Use of Force etc.**
 
• Types of Dictatorships are:
 
 
• **Totalitarian Dictatorship**: where the government seeks to control all aspects of public and private life (e.g., North Korea)
 
• **Authoritarian Dictatorship**: Power is concentrated in a single leader or ruling party, but some limited social and economic freedoms may exist (e.g., Russia under Vladimir Putin).
 
• **Military Dictatorship**: The military controls the government (e.g., Myanmar).
 
• **Personalist Dictatorship**: The leader maintains power primarily through personal loyalty (e.g., Saddam Hussein's Iraq).
 
 
 
• An **autocracy** is a form of government in which one individual holds absolute power and authority over the state, often without constitutional accountability.
 
• Key features of Autocracy includes: **Centralized Authority**, **Lack of Political Pluralism**, **Limited Civil Liberties, U****naccountability**, **State Control of Institutions. **
 
• Types of autocracy includes: 
 
 
• **Absolute Monarchy**: A hereditary ruler holds complete power (e.g., Saudi Arabia). The monarch has no constitutional limits on their authority.
 
• **Dictatorship**: Similar to autocracy, where a single leader (dictator) maintains control through force or manipulation (e.g., North Korea under Kim Jong-un).
 
• **Personalist Regime**: Power is centered around a single leader who relies on personal loyalty rather than institutional structures (e.g., Zimbabwe under Robert Mugabe).

questions.question: Right to freedom of speech and expression is given under:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 19.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 19 is not completely absolute. It also impose some reasonable restrictions.
 
• The right includes:
 
 
• Right to Propagate One's Views.
 
• Right to Information.
 
• Freedom of the Press.
 
• Right to Criticize Government.
 
• Commercial Speech.
 
 
 
• Article 19(2) allows the state to impose reasonable restrictions on certain grounds. Such as:
 
 
• Sovereignty and Integrity of India.
 
• Security of the State.
 
• Friendly Relations with Foreign States.
 
• Public Order.
 
• Decency or Morality.
 
• Contempt of Court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 20 **of the Indian Constitution provides protection in respect of conviction for offenses.
 
• **Article 20(1) **protects individuals from being punished under laws that are created and enforced after the alleged act has been committed.
 
• **Article 20(2) **states that No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once.
 
• **Article 20(3) **states that No person shall be compelled to be a witness against themselves. 
 
• This provides the right to remain silent, ensuring that an accused person cannot be forced to confess guilt through coercion or compulsion. 
 
• **Article 30 **of the Indian Constitution provides specific rights to religious and linguistic minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• **Article 30(1) **states that All minorities, whether based on religion or language, have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution is a cornerstone of the country’s democratic framework, providing the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar **referred to Article 32 as the **heart and soul** of the Indian Constitution because it ensures the protection and enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• **Article 32(1)**** **states that Every individual has the right to directly approach the Supreme Court to seek remedies if they believe their fundamental rights have been violated.
 
• **Article 32(2)**** **states that The Supreme Court shall have power to issue directions or orders or writs. These writs include:
 
 
• ​**Mandamus**: A writ directed at any public authority to perform a duty they are legally obligated to complete.
 
• **Habeas Corpus**: used to bring a person who has been detained unlawfully before the court to determine if their detention is legal.
 
• **Prohibition**: A writ directed to a lower court or tribunal to cease proceedings that exceed their jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari**: A writ issued to quash an order or decision of a lower court or tribunal due to lack of jurisdiction, error of law, or breach of natural justice.
 
• **Quo Warranto**: A writ questioning the authority of a person to hold a public office.
 
 
 
• **Article 32(3) **states that Parliament has the authority to empower other courts to issue directions or orders or writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights within their local jurisdictions.
 
• 
 
**Article 32(4) **states that The right guaranteed by this article shall not be suspended except as otherwise provided for by this Constitution.

questions.question: In __________, the Planning Commission was set up with the Prime Minister as its Chairperson.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1950__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Planning Commission was set up on **March 15, 1950.**
 
• It is headed by **Prime Minister **of India.
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru **was the first Chairperson of the Planning Commission.
 
• It was a **non-constitutional body **formed for assessing the country’s resources and developing plans for their effective and balanced utilization. 
 
• Some key tasks includes: Formulation of Five-Year Plans, Resource Allocation, Continuous Evaluation, Policy Advisory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by **NITI Aayog **on **January 1, 2015.**
 
• The council includes: 
 
 
• **Governing Council**: Includes the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers of all states, and administrators of Union Territories.
 
• **Vice-Chairperson and Members**: Appointed by the Prime Minister.
 
• **Full-Time Members**: Often experts in various fields.
 
• **Special Invitees:** Subject matter experts and eminent professionals as required for specific issues.
 
 
 
• It is formed to provide: 
 
 
• **Fostering Cooperative Federalism**: Strengthening states by participation in planning and development.
 
• **Dynamic Role**: acting as a think tank and policy advisor.
 
• **Bottom-Up Approach**: focus on collaboration at the grassroots level and local governance.
 
• **Performance Monitoring**: Detailed monitoring and evaluation of implemented policies.
 
 
 
• NITI Aayog is more functional tha Planning Commission because:
 
 
• Promotes a **bottom-up approach, **emphasizing cooperative federalism.
 
• Acts as a **dynamic think tank **that can respond quickly to changing circumstances.
 
• uses **real-time data and analytics **to assess progress and recommends corrective measures, ensuring accountability and efficiency.
 
• Encourages **innovation and entrepreneurship **through initiatives like **the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM).**
 
• Comprised of experts in various fields, facilitating more informed policy recommendations.
 
• Utilizes **modern technology and big data analytics **for policy development and monitoring.

questions.question: Which of the following device is used to measure the distance travelled by the vehicle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The device used to measure the distance traveled by a vehicle is called an odometer. 
 
• Odometers can be mechanical, electronic, or a combination of both, and they provide a reading of the total distance traveled by a vehicle.
 
• **Mechanical** Odometers: These use a series of gears and cogs to turn the reading on a dial as the vehicle moves.
 
• **Digital** Odometers: These are electronic and display the reading on a screen. They are often found in modern vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: According to the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), the unemployment rate for individuals aged 15 years and above in urban areas decreased to ________ during January-March 2023 from 8.2 percent a year ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.8**__%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The unemployment rate for people aged 15 years and above in urban areas **fell to 6.8%.**
 
• **The Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), **of the population aged 15 years and above,** increased to 48.5% **in January-March 2023.
 
• **The Worker Population Ratio (WPR),** defined as the percentage of employed individuals in the population aged 15 years and above,** rose to 45.2%.**
 
• The data was collected as part of the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**, which is conducted by the NSSO.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **unemployment rate among males in urban areas decreased to 6.0%** in January-March 2023 from 7.7% a year ago.
 
• The** unemployment rate among females in urban areas dropped to 9.2% **during the same period, down from 10.1% in January-March 2022.
 
• The **Work Participation Rate (WPR) **is defined as the percentage of workers in the total population.in **2011 was 39.8%**.
 
• **Main Workers** constituted 30.4% of the population.
 
• **Marginal Workers** constituted 9.4% of the population.
 
• **In rural areas, the WPR was 41.8%**, with a higher proportion of workers involved in agriculture and related activities.
 
• **In urban areas, the WPR was 35.3%,** with more people involved in non-agricultural sectors like services, trade, and manufacturing.
 
• **Non-workers **(those not engaged in any economically productive activity) accounted for approximately **60.2% of the population.**

questions.question: In November 2023, which Indian skydiver jumped from a helicopter from a height of 21,500 feet in front of the world's highest peak Mount Everest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shital Mahajan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In November 2023, Shital Mahajan, an Indian skydiver, made a remarkable jump from a helicopter at an altitude of** 21,500 feet in front of Mount Everest.**
 
• Shital Mahajan was born on September 19, 1982, in **Pune, Maharashtra, India**.
 
• In 2004, at the age of 23, Shital Mahajan became the** first woman** to perform a skydiving **jump over both the North Pole and South Pole.**
 
• Shital Mahajan was awarded the** Padma Shri,** one of India's highest civilian honors, in **2011**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• She received the **Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award**, which is India's highest honor for adventure sports.
 
• Apart from Guinness World Records, her achievements are also recognized by the **Limca Book of Records**, which has featured her for her skydiving feats.
 
• Mount Everest's official height is **8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 feet) **above sea level. This was confirmed by a 2020 survey conducted by China and Nepal.
 
• Everest is part of the Himalayan mountain range, located on the border between **Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.**
 
• The** first successful ascent** of Mount Everest was made on May 29, 1953, by **Sir Edmund Hillary of New Zealand **and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa of Nepal.
 
• The** youngest person **to summit Everest is **Jordan Romero, who was 13 years old **when he reached the top in 2010.
 
• Everest is still growing at a rate of about **4 millimeters per year** due to tectonic activity between the Indian and Eurasian plates.

questions.question: The term "CRR" in the context of Indian banking stands for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cash Reserve Ratio.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** is the amount of money banks have to keep with the Reserve Bank of India as liquid cash. 
 
• It's a way for the RBI to ensure banks have enough cash in hand.
 
• CRR is used by the **RBI to control liquidity in the banking system.**
 
• By adjusting the CRR, the RBI can influence the amount of money available for lending, thereby controlling inflation and stabilizing the economy.
 
• **Current Rate: **As of now, the CRR is set at 4.50%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Credit Rating Regulation** refers to the **rules and standards that credit rating agencies must follow** to make sure their ratings of financial products, companies, or governments are clear, accurate, and reliable. These regulations help maintain trust in the financial markets by ensuring that credit ratings are based on solid analysis and transparent processes.
 
• The** Capital Recovery Rate is a financial measure that shows how quickly an investment recovers** its initial cost. It helps investors understand how long it will take for them to get back the money they put into an investment.
 
• **Consumer Rights and Responsibilities** refer to the rights consumers have to fair treatment, safety, and information in the marketplace, and the responsibilities they must follow, such as being informed and making ethical choices.

• Nathuram Mirdha was a distinguished** freedom fighter and a prominent leader of the farming community.**
 
• His legacy includes serving as a **Union Minister and being elected six times to the Lok Sabha.**
 
• The ceremony highlighted Mirdha’s significant contributions to social work and his enduring vision for the farming community, celebrating his lifelong dedication to improving the lives of farmers and advocating for their rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jagdeep Dhankhar **(since August 11, 2022), affiliated with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• The Vice President is the** ex officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha** (Council of States), the upper house of India’s Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: In _________, the All India Kabaddi Federation came into existence and compiled standard rules.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1950.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The All-India Kabaddi Federation was established in 1950.
 
• It aimed to promote and organize Kabaddi at a national level.
 
• The federation started organizing national-level competitions, including the Senior National Championship from 1952.
 
• The federation compiled and standardized the rules of Kabaddi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in ancient India.
 
• There are seven players in a team.

 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 

 Raider
 The player who enters the opponent’s half to tag defenders and score points.
 
 

 Cant
 The continuous chant of “kabaddi” by the raider during the raid.
 
 

 Super Tackle
 A tackle executed by three or fewer defenders, earning the defending team an extra point.
 
 

 Do or Die Raid
 A raid where the raider must score a point; failing to do so results in the raider being out.
 
 

 All Out
 When all players of a team are out, the opposing team earns additional points and all players are revived.
 
 

 Bonus Line
 A line that, when crossed by the raider with at least one foot in the air, awards an extra point.
 
 

 Pursuit
 A move where a defender chases and attempts to tag the raider immediately after the raider has completed their raid.

questions.question: Who was founder of the Agra Gharana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khuda Baksh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Khuda Baksh **was a prominent musician and the founder of the **Agra Gharana**.
 
• The Agra Gharana is one of the **main vocal styles** or 'gharanas' of Hindustani classical music.
 
• Khuda Baksh's style emphasized the use of powerful and robust vocal techniques.
 
• The Agra Gharana evolved from the 'Dhrupad' tradition and later incorporated elements of 'Khayal' singing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agra Gharana**

 
 
• The Agra Gharana is known for its emphasis on rhythm and the use of a wide range of vocal techniques and improvisations.
 
• This gharana has produced many illustrious musicians who have made significant contributions to Indian classical music.
 
• The singing style of this gharana is characterized by the use of 'nom-tom' alaaps, which are a form of vocal improvisation.
 
• The Agra Gharana has a rich repertoire of compositions, including '**bandishes**' (fixed compositions) in different ragas.
 
 
 
• **Dhrupad**
 
 
• Dhrupad is one of the oldest forms of **Hindustani classical music **and is known for its spiritual and solemn nature.
 
• It places a strong emphasis on maintaining the purity of the raga and the use of precise and intricate rhythmic patterns.
 
• The compositions in Dhrupad are usually devotional or heroic in nature.
 
• Dhrupad is traditionally accompanied by the '**pakhawaj**', a barrel-shaped drum.
 
 
 
• **Khayal**
 
 
• Khayal is a more modern form of **Hindustani classical music **compared to Dhrupad and is known for its expressiveness and flexibility.
 
• It allows for a greater degree of improvisation and emotional expression.
 
• Khayal compositions are typically shorter than Dhrupad compositions and are often based on romantic or devotional themes.
 
• Khayal singing is usually accompanied by the '**tabla**' and '**harmonium**' or '**sarangi**'.

questions.question: Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry is associated with which of the following dance style?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry is a renowned figure associated with the Kuchipudi dance style.
 
• He comes from a long line of traditional Kuchipudi gurus and has been instrumental in preserving and promoting this classical dance form.
 
• **Kuchipudi is a classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh**, known for its graceful movements, dramatic expressions, and unique style of storytelling through dance.
 
• Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry has contributed to the evolution of Kuchipudi by blending traditional and contemporary elements.
 
• His family has been deeply rooted in the development of Kuchipudi as a prominent classical dance form in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/989639b1181533b1a52253c99330e69cd1ab2906344963d4ebcc7c80bc3ddc01.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya:**

 
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance form from** Assam.**
 
• It was traditionally performed by monks in monasteries (Sattras) as part of their devotion to Lord Vishnu.
 
• It is not related to Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry.
 
 
 
• **Bharatnatyam:**
 
 
• Bharatnatyam is a classical dance form from **Tamil Nadu.**
 
• It emphasizes fixed upper torso, intricate footwork, and expressive hand gestures.
 
• While it is one of the most famous dance forms in India, it is not linked to Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry.
 
 
 
• **Kathak:**
 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance style from **North India**, associated with storytelling through rhythmic foot movements and spins.
 
• It originated from the traveling bards of ancient northern India.
 
• Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry is not associated with this dance form.

questions.question: Jawara dance is a popular folk dance of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Jawara dance is a popular folk dance of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is mainly performed in the Bundelkhand region of the state.
 
• The dance celebrates a good harvest, symbolizing joy and prosperity among the farming communities.
 
• Participants perform this dance with baskets full of crops, primarily jawara (barley), on their heads.
 
• The lively music and rhythmic movements express the happiness of the farmers after a successful harvest.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a1794053179a00075131356025b5e331f22731b18858f6e45928e66afa190075.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kerala:**

 
 
• Kerala is known for classical dance forms like** Kathakali and Mohiniyattam** rather than folk dances like Jawara.
 
• The state's folk culture includes Kummattikali and Thiruvathira, but they are distinct from Jawara.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh has folk dances like **Nati and Kullu Nati**, performed during festivals and cultural events.
 
• Jawara is not associated with this region.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat:**
 
 
• Gujarat is famous for its folk dances like **Garba and Dandiya**, which are performed during Navratri and other celebrations.
 
• Jawara dance is not part of Gujarat's folk traditions.

questions.question: The languages spoken in Jharkhand and parts of central India mainly belong to which of the following language family?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Austro-Asiatic family.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The languages spoken in **Jharkhand and parts of central India,** especially among tribal communities, mainly belong to the Austro-Asiatic language family.
 
• Munda languages, such as** Santali, Mundari, and Ho**, are part of this family and are widely spoken in these regions.
 
• These languages have ancient roots and are primarily spoken by indigenous and tribal populations.
 
• The Austro-Asiatic family is one of the earliest language families in India, distinct from the other dominant language families.
 
• Jharkhand is known for its** linguistic diversity**, but the Austro-Asiatic languages form a significant part of the state's cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-European family:**

 
 
• This family includes major languages like **Hindi, Bengali, and Marathi**, but it is not predominant among the tribal communities of Jharkhand.
 
• It is the largest language family in India, but Austro-Asiatic languages are more common in central India's tribal regions.
 
 
 
• **Tibeto-Burman family:**
 
 
• This family is found in northeastern India, primarily in states like **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, and Manipur.**
 
• It does not have significant representation in Jharkhand or central India.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian family:**
 
 
• Dravidian languages, such as **Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam,** are predominantly spoken in southern India.
 
• While some Dravidian-speaking communities exist in central India, the Austro-Asiatic family is more relevant to Jharkhand.
